text:
mira: anyone else seeing intermittent east-west drops in us-west-gpu this morning? ~1-2% pod-to-pod packet loss correlated with bursts of pod churn / backfills.
raj: yup, seen a spike in gRPC retransmits from model-serving pods around 03:10-03:25 UTC. mostly between node-pool-b nodes.
mira: tcpdump quick capture shows a burst pattern on VXLAN UDP 4789, a bunch of small fragmented UDP packets then some are missing. ran: `tcpdump -nn -i bond0 udp and port 4789` and saw sequences like "IP (frag 1/2)" then gaps.
elaine: could be MTU / offload mismatch. are host NIC offloads enabled? `ethtool -k` on affected hosts?
mira: ethtool shows gso/gro/tx-checksumming enabled on the physical NICs. we haven't touched MTU recently (9000).
ops-bot: GPU-autoscaler triggered scale-down: removed nodes: gpu-usw-3a-{12,13,14,15} at 2024-11-12T03:12:07Z.
nate: also pulled some data from leaf switches — saw VXLAN rewrite table spike and a short window where entries were being aged/evicted. could be neighbor churn combined with encap path thrash. CCing network.
marco: can you paste `ip -s link show vxlan0` from an affected host? curious about RX/TX/drop counters on the overlay device.
mira: paste: `vxlan0: RX packets 1,234, errors 0, dropped 56, overruns 0, frame 0; TX packets 1,220, dropped 0` — drops only on RX.
raj: that smells like the kernel dropping reassembled frames when offload/GRO interacts with encapsulation. try toggling GRO/GSO on vxlan interface: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off` and re-run short load.
mira: applying now on one problematic host… doing a 10m smoke of model-serving traffic.
mira: quick update — after disabling GRO/GSO on vxlan0, retransmits dropped a lot: loss down to ~0.1% in the next 20m sampling window.
elaine: interesting — points to offload + fragmentation race during high churn. kernel sometimes hands fragmented skbs to GSO/GRO path and they get dropped when encapsulation metadata changes.
nate: also correlates with switch rewrite thrash — when the leaf is evicting entries, packets might be punted to host and get re-encapsulated; combined with offloads can cause boundary cases.
marco: good repro step then: trigger scale-down/backfill on a small canary pool with vxlan GRO enabled vs disabled and compare. can we also capture `skb` drops counters?
mira: will run canary test and collect `dmesg` + `ip -s link` + tcpdump. filing a short follow-up ticket TICKET-3421 and will attach captures.
elaine: action items: 1) run controlled repro on 3 nodes (w/ and w/out vxlan GRO) 2) add a systemd unit to enforce `ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off` on affected AMIs if repro holds 3) open vendor NIC bug with captures + switch rewrite logs.
raj: :thumbsup: sounds good. if we see consistent improvement, push AMI change and include note in release notes.
ate: i'll pull switch rewrite logs for the 03:10 window and add to the ticket.
mira: thanks all — will post results in this thread once the canary run completes.
ops-bot: runbook note: escalation to net-eng recommended when overlay rewrite churn correlates with drops.
